runs.content: Wednesday's rotation focus is Health + Learning. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-08), log.md shows no new activity at all beyond the scheduled end-of-day memory update — a genuinely quiet window. Deep-reading Health's overview, my-protocol, and both source pages (Wood on brain health, Godin on breathwork), plus Learning's previously-unexamined pages (framework-empathy-worldview, framework-enrollment, the two Kevin Kelly source pages, Dave Gray's empathy map, and person-seth-godin), turned up one genuinely new, non-duplicate investigation idea: raw/learning/ holds a full 1,469-line Diary of a CEO transcript (Chris Koerner, 'king of side hustles,' 80+ businesses started) tagged `ingested` since April 2026 that was never actually turned into a wiki page anywhere — no Learning source page, no podcasts/ entry (unlike the four other Diary of a CEO episodes already ingested), no index.md row. Koerner's own answer to 'Is This the Best Time to Start a Business?' ('every day that goes by, the timing gets better... there are more tools than ever') is close to a word-for-word 2026 restatement of Kevin Kelly's 2014 'You Are Not Late' thesis already sitting in the wiki (learning/source-kelly-you-are-not-late), which neither page currently reflects. No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today — the closest candidate (Seth Godin bridging Learning and Health as an unlinked author across person-seth-godin.md and health/source-godin-breathwork-2026.md) turned out to already be logged as an open idea from 2026-07-08, still unresolved but not new. Nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution — Health's my-protocol.md is still 100% placeholder tables, unchanged since May.

Tuesday's rotation focus is AI & Tech + Technology. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-07), log.md shows only routine automated Finance activity (a growth-value-tracker refresh, a portfolio-management-briefing, and a no-trade Labor Day paper-trading entry) with nothing new in AI & Tech or Technology to review — memory/index.md's Domain Content Status for both domains is unchanged since the last deep-dive. Deep-reading the AI & Tech and Technology overview pages plus a handful of previously-unexamined source pages in both domains (Blodget's AI-bubble piece, the Nvidia $500bn backstop/Theseus Infrastructure digest, SemiAnalysis's CXMT writeup, and Technology's GitHub Copilot and Meta-AI-briefing source pages) surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connection: GitHub Copilot's June 2026 switch to token-based billing (technology/source-github-copilot-token-billing-2026 — developers seeing $29-to-$750+/month cost jumps, concentrated specifically in 'multi-agent, long-running tasks') is a live, dated, consumer-facing instance of exactly the token-cost-adoption-barrier Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora's piece (ai-tech/source-arora-token-pricing-2026-07-09) treats as a forward-looking constraint five weeks later — Arora's own reference catalyst is specifically 'agentic coding' token efficiency, the same product category Copilot's backlash sits in. Neither page cites the other; the Technology-domain source page only cross-links to its own domain overview. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today (candidates considered — the Theseus Infrastructure JV's consumer-electricity-price-guarantee term, and Fred's own Claude Code cost exposure — were either already covered by existing open threads or too speculative to state as a concrete next step), and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.
